newsitem.title: CHINA: China to demand insurance for accident-hit miners.
newsitem.headline: China to demand insurance for accident-hit miners.

text.p: China's disaster-plagued coal mines will be forced to buy accident insurance for their miners under rules to be introduced from July 1, the China Daily said on Thursday.

Officials were putting the final touches to regulations that would make it mandatory for all coal-mining companies to provide the coverage for their workers, the newspaper quoted Wang Xiaoqi of the Ministry of Coal Industry as saying.

The coal mining sector suffered the highest death toll and the most injuries of all Chinese industries, but compensation was paid to miners and their families according to rules that were more than 40 years old, Wang said.
Under the new regulations, relatives of miners killed in accidents would receive about 50,000 yuan ($6,000), more than 20 times the current amount, he said.

Insurance premiums would range from 20-30 yuan a year, but insurance fees would continue to be inadequate because the coal industry as a whole was still suffering economic losses, he said but gave no details.
The rules, to come into force on July 1, were in accordance with a coal mining law issued last year, he said.
Explosions and other accidents kill up to 10,000 Chinese miners a year, with coal mines accounting for more than a third of the total, government statistics show.
Last month, 86 miners were killed by a series of explosions that ripped through three privately run coal mines in central China.
The disaster happened just a month after Beijing vowed to sack the managers of coal mines that suffered serous accidents and to launch reforms to boost safety, efficiency and economic returns.
